subject: System Design
title: The Problem with Physical Clocks
description: A fast breakdown of The Problem with Physical Clocks for builders.

hook.text: Server A's clock says 10:00:00.000. Server B's clock says 10:00:00.032. Which write happened first?

buildup.text: Physical clocks on different machines drift apart. NTP synchronizes them but only to within milliseconds.

discovery.text: Google's Spanner uses GPS and atomic clocks to keep servers within 7 microseconds of each other.

twist.text: Most companies don't have GPS clocks. Clock drift of 100ms is common and can silently corrupt data ordering.

climax.text: Using wall-clock timestamps for ordering in distributed systems is fundamentally unreliable.

punchline.text: Distributed clocks drift — don't trust timestamps for ordering.

quiz.question: Why are physical clocks unreliable for ordering events?
options: Clocks on different machines drift apart by milliseconds
